newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodian opposition politicians held in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian opposition politicians held in Thailand.

text.p: Thai immigration officials arrested seven Cambodian opposition politicians who fled illegally across the border into Thailand, officials said on Thursday.

Seven members of Sam Rainsy's Khmer Nation Party (KNP) were detained by police late on Wednesday as they tried to cross from the Cambodian border town of Poipet to this eastern Thai town to escape troops loyal to strongman Hun Sen enter Poipet.

The seven were among a group of KNP supporters who had earlier fled the capital Phnom Penh because they feared repression by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who ousted First Prime Minster Norodom Ranariddh in a coup on July 6.

"I am a colleague of Sam Rainsy's and I ran away from Phnom Penh to Poipet. Yesterday, when I saw Hun Sen's soldiers in Poipet, we got scared and ran away to Thailand," So Chan Dara, leader of the group, told Reuters.
Hun Sen's forces came to a power-sharing agreement with royalist troops who controlled this town and Hun Sen's men began to enter Poipet on Wednesday.

After seeing the troops enter town, the seven men tried to cross the border by following a set of train tracks linking the two countries about four hours after the border checkpoint was closed on Wednesday.
Thai police said they detained the men for illegal entry and said they were investigating to see if they were really politicians or illegal migrant workers seeking jobs in Thailand.
They were due to go to court on Friday and then would likely be returned to Poipet, police said.

Sam Rainsy was detained briefly by Thai police on Wednesday as he attempted to cross from Thailand into Poipet. He had planned to meet 52 KNP supporters who were holed up in Poipet waiting to flee the country along with about 300 members of the FUNCINPEC party of the ousted First Prime Minister, Prince Norodom Ranariddh's
A Thai army officer said Sam Rainsy had caused trouble for Thailand by using its soil for an uprising against the Cambodian government.
Sam Rainsy, who is allied with FUNCINPEC, has called for international pressure to force Hun Sen to step down.
